subject: Finding cause of latency in client-server communication

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Finding cause of latency in client-server communication
parts:
Sometimes in my shiny app there appears to be a very high latency in the feedback from the server. Both the R code that handles the calculations and sends the data to the client, as well as the client-side javascript code has been timed and it does not account for the long response time - furthermore it appears at random, sometimes not showing at all and after a short period happening in the exact same use case.

My theory is that either the communication between client and server is being throttled somehow, or that the shiny R-session process somehow needs to wake up now and then(?), but I don't know how to investigate this further...

I'm on a mac btw, and this is only related to running apps locally (since it has not been deployed on a server yet)

best

Thomas

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Re: Finding cause of latency in client-server communication
parts:
I just updated most of my app to use session$sendCustomMessage() instead of relying on custom outputs to send data to the client. This seems to remove the problem. My theory is that the overhead of the reactive paradigm used in Shiny can become quite large when the dependency graph has to be recreated - maybe this is only a problem when large amount of data is send to the client, which is why most people don't experience it (I routinely send +10mb data chunks to the client)

If someone from Shiny development could elaborate it would be cool : )

best

Thomas

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Finding cause of latency in client-server communication
parts:
Might the issue be that all outputs are held and "flushed" at the same time? In other words, if a new value for input x is sent from the client, and outputs a, b, and c all depend (directly or indirectly) on it, then they are all executed serially but only sent to the client when the last one completes. This is in contrast to sendCustomMessage, which goes immediately. (I was always prepared for this to be a controversial decision and we could do work to make this a per-output option, but it comes up surprisingly little)

The work required to maintain the reactive graph is miniscule in most cases, and shouldn't be related to the size of the data being sent around.

messages.author: 85435c7e2689700c
messages.subject: Re: Finding cause of latency in client-server communication
parts:
Thanks for the response Joe

I don't think that what you describe at least are fully responsible for my issues. In my case only one 'response' is generated once an input is updated, so there is nothing to wait for. After timing my app some more I can say that the problem is not fully gone. Before changing to sendCustomMessage the problem would be in the form of 'lag - R computation - lag'. Now it is 'lag - R computation', so only the last part of the latency is gone.

Also, the perplexing thing is that the exact same operation (e.g. clicking on the same option in a select list) can sometimes have a lag, and sometimes not. The only unifying aspect is that I have only seen the behavior in very data-intense apps...

Will some of you RStudio guys be at the Bioconductor conference since you are a sponsor? In that case it might be easier to sort this out face-to-face?

best

Thomas
